name: Grid Movement Range
description: The blue tiles. Given a unit's position and movement budget this computes the reachable set — flood fill over world.tile_grid with per-terrain costs and obstacle blocking — plus the attack overlay derived from it, because move-then-shoot range is a union of tiles, not a circle. world.tile_grid owns the board and movement.pathfinding_system can find A path; this component owns the budget question — ALL paths within N points — which is why it sits on top of both instead of replacing either. It deliberately knows nothing about whose turn it is: combat.turn_order_queue announces the active unit, and this answers for whoever that is, player or AI alike.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: terrainCostTable
inputs.description: Movement-point cost per terrain tag. 99 is the polite infinity: technically crossable, never actually reached.

inputs.name: diagonalMovementCost
inputs.description: Cost of a diagonal step. 1.5 approximates real distance; 1 makes diagonals strictly better, which quietly warps every formation.

inputs.name: zoneOfControl
inputs.description: Whether stepping adjacent to an enemy ends movement. ZoC is what makes frontlines frontlines; without it, every melee unit is a revolving door.

inputs.name: showAttackOverlay
inputs.description: Whether the attackable set is computed alongside the reachable set. Off only for games where attacks are strictly adjacent.

outputs.name: reachableTiles
outputs.description: Tiles the active unit can stop on this turn.

outputs.name: attackableTiles
outputs.description: Tiles targetable after any legal move — the red tiles.
